title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.17963v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. In current discourse around ''world models,'' their attainment is framed as the achievement of internal consistency, cross-modal alignment, and physical grounding. Taken together, these demands converge on an ideal of the model as a universal translation machine capable of establishing lossless correspondences across linguistic, visual, and physical representation spaces. I show that this ideal presupposes a metaphysical commitment that I call a statistical ontology: the belief that reality has an underlying, computable statistical structure that can be recovered through sufficient data and modeling, rather than being shaped and accessed through situated human interpretation and labor. translated_title: 迈向普遍可译性：论生成式人工智能的统计本体论
translated_abstract: 本文论证，翻译问题既构成了当代生成式人工智能的起点，也是其规范性视界。在当前围绕“世界模型”的讨论中，世界模型的实现被框定为内部一致性、跨模态对齐与物理接地的达成。这些要求汇聚成一种理想：将模型视为一台通用翻译机器，能够在语言、视觉与物理表征空间之间建立无损的对应关系。本文指出，这一理想预设了一种形而上学承诺，作者称之为“统计本体论”：即相信现实具有一种潜在的、可计算的统计结构，可以通过充足的数据与建模加以恢复，而非通过情境化的人类诠释与劳动来塑造和通达。通过将这一承诺追溯至沃伦·韦弗1949年关于机器翻译的备忘录，本文勾勒了翻译如何……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出翻译是当代生成式AI的起点与规范目标，其“通用翻译机器”理想背后隐含一种可追溯至韦弗1949年机器翻译备忘录的“统计本体论”形而上学承诺——即相信现实具有可通过数据与建模恢复的可计算统计结构。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that translation serves as both the origin and normative horizon of contemporary generative AI, whose ideal of a "universal translation machine" presupposes a metaphysical commitment it terms "statistical ontology"—traceable to Warren Weaver's 1949 memorandum—namely, the belief that reality possesses a computable statistical structure recoverable through sufficient data and modeling.
